data.scenario_text: The function f(x)=14\sin\left[\frac{\pi}{6}(x-4)\right]+47 models the average monthly temperature, in degrees Fahrenheit, for a particular city, where x=1 represents January, x=2 represents February, and so on.

data.part_d: What is the phase shift of this function, and what does it mean in this context?
data.part_e: Use the model to estimate the average temperature in May. Round to the nearest tenth of a degree.
data.solution_steps:
Part (a). The midline of a sinusoid f(x)=A\sin[B(x-h)]+D is y=D, and the midline is the average value of the oscillation. Here D=47, so the average temperature is \boxed{47^\circ\text{F}}.

Part (b). The amplitude is A=14, so the quantity rises 14 above the average value and falls 14 below it:

\text{maximum}=47+14=61^\circ\text{F}\qquad\text{minimum}=47-14=33^\circ\text{F}

The warmest month on average is July and the coolest is January, so the range of monthly average temperatures is \boxed{[33^\circ\text{F},\ 61^\circ\text{F}]}.

Part (c). Here B=\frac{\pi}{6}, so the period is

\text{Period}=\frac{2\pi}{B}=\frac{2\pi}{\pi/6}=2\pi\cdot\frac{6}{\pi}=12

The period is \boxed{12} months, and so the temperature pattern repeats every 12 months, that is, once each year.

Part (d). The phase shift is the value of x that makes the argument of the sine equal to zero:

\frac{\pi}{6}(x-4)=0 \implies x-4=0 \implies x=4

The phase shift is \boxed{4} months, and so the sine pattern is shifted 4 months to the right: the temperature is at its average and rising in April, not in January. Equivalently, the warmest month is July and the coolest is January.

Part (e). Substitute x=5 (May):

f(5)=14\sin\left[\frac{\pi}{6}(5-4)\right]+47=14\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)+47

=14\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)+47=54

So the model gives exactly \boxed{54.0^\circ\text{F}} in May.

data.part_d: What is the phase shift of this function, and what does it mean in this context?
data.part_e: Use the model to estimate the average temperature in July. Round to the nearest tenth of a degree.
data.solution_steps:
Part (a). The midline of a sinusoid f(x)=A\sin[B(x-h)]+D is y=D, and the midline is the average value of the oscillation. Here D=61, so the average temperature is \boxed{61^\circ\text{F}}.

Part (b). The amplitude is A=20, so the quantity rises 20 above the average value and falls 20 below it:

\text{maximum}=61+20=81^\circ\text{F}\qquad\text{minimum}=61-20=41^\circ\text{F}

The warmest month on average is May and the coolest is November, so the range of monthly average temperatures is \boxed{[41^\circ\text{F},\ 81^\circ\text{F}]}.

Part (c). Here B=\frac{\pi}{6}, so the period is

\text{Period}=\frac{2\pi}{B}=\frac{2\pi}{\pi/6}=2\pi\cdot\frac{6}{\pi}=12

The period is \boxed{12} months, and so the temperature pattern repeats every 12 months, that is, once each year.

Part (d). The phase shift is the value of x that makes the argument of the sine equal to zero:

\frac{\pi}{6}(x-2)=0 \implies x-2=0 \implies x=2

The phase shift is \boxed{2} months, and so the sine pattern is shifted 2 months to the right: the temperature is at its average and rising in February, not in January. Equivalently, the warmest month is May and the coolest is November.

Part (e). Substitute x=7 (July):

f(7)=20\sin\left[\frac{\pi}{6}(7-2)\right]+61=20\sin\left(\frac{5\pi}{6}\right)+61

=20\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)+61=71

So the model gives exactly \boxed{71.0^\circ\text{F}} in July.

Part (a). The midline of a sinusoid f(x)=A\sin[B(x-h)]+D is y=D, and the midline is the average value of the oscillation. Here D=62, so the average temperature is \boxed{62^\circ\text{F}}.

Part (b). The amplitude is A=12, so the quantity rises 12 above the average value and falls 12 below it:

\text{maximum}=62+12=74^\circ\text{F}\qquad\text{minimum}=62-12=50^\circ\text{F}

The warmest month on average is July and the coolest is January, so the range of monthly average temperatures is \boxed{[50^\circ\text{F},\ 74^\circ\text{F}]}.

Part (c). Here B=\frac{\pi}{6}, so the period is

\text{Period}=\frac{2\pi}{B}=\frac{2\pi}{\pi/6}=2\pi\cdot\frac{6}{\pi}=12

The period is \boxed{12} months, and so the temperature pattern repeats every 12 months, that is, once each year.

data.part_c: What is the period of this function, and what does it mean in this context?
data.part_d: What is the phase shift of this function, and what does it mean in this context?
data.part_e: Use the model to estimate the average temperature in July. Round to the nearest tenth of a degree.
data.solution_steps:
Part (a). The midline of a sinusoid f(x)=A\sin[B(x-h)]+D is y=D, and the midline is the average value of the oscillation. Here D=48, so the average temperature is \boxed{48^\circ\text{F}}.

Part (b). The amplitude is A=22, so the quantity rises 22 above the average value and falls 22 below it:

\text{maximum}=48+22=70^\circ\text{F}\qquad\text{minimum}=48-22=26^\circ\text{F}

The warmest month on average is May and the coolest is November, so the range of monthly average temperatures is \boxed{[26^\circ\text{F},\ 70^\circ\text{F}]}.

Part (c). Here B=\frac{\pi}{6}, so the period is

\text{Period}=\frac{2\pi}{B}=\frac{2\pi}{\pi/6}=2\pi\cdot\frac{6}{\pi}=12

The period is \boxed{12} months, and so the temperature pattern repeats every 12 months, that is, once each year.

Part (d). The phase shift is the value of x that makes the argument of the sine equal to zero:

\frac{\pi}{6}(x-2)=0 \implies x-2=0 \implies x=2

The phase shift is \boxed{2} months, and so the sine pattern is shifted 2 months to the right: the temperature is at its average and rising in February, not in January. Equivalently, the warmest month is May and the coolest is November.

Part (e). Substitute x=7 (July):

f(7)=22\sin\left[\frac{\pi}{6}(7-2)\right]+48=22\sin\left(\frac{5\pi}{6}\right)+48

=22\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)+48=59

So the model gives exactly \boxed{59.0^\circ\text{F}} in July.

data.part_c: What is the period of this function, and what does it mean in this context?
data.part_d: What is the phase shift of this function, and what does it mean in this context?
data.part_e: Use the model to estimate the average temperature in April. Round to the nearest tenth of a degree.
data.solution_steps:
Part (a). The midline of a sinusoid f(x)=A\sin[B(x-h)]+D is y=D, and the midline is the average value of the oscillation. Here D=48, so the average temperature is \boxed{48^\circ\text{F}}.

Part (b). The amplitude is A=22, so the quantity rises 22 above the average value and falls 22 below it:

\text{maximum}=48+22=70^\circ\text{F}\qquad\text{minimum}=48-22=26^\circ\text{F}

The warmest month on average is May and the coolest is November, so the range of monthly average temperatures is \boxed{[26^\circ\text{F},\ 70^\circ\text{F}]}.

Part (c). Here B=\frac{\pi}{6}, so the period is

\text{Period}=\frac{2\pi}{B}=\frac{2\pi}{\pi/6}=2\pi\cdot\frac{6}{\pi}=12

The period is \boxed{12} months, and so the temperature pattern repeats every 12 months, that is, once each year.

Part (d). The phase shift is the value of x that makes the argument of the sine equal to zero:

\frac{\pi}{6}(x-2)=0 \implies x-2=0 \implies x=2

The phase shift is \boxed{2} months, and so the sine pattern is shifted 2 months to the right: the temperature is at its average and rising in February, not in January. Equivalently, the warmest month is May and the coolest is November.

Part (e). Substitute x=4 (April):

f(4)=22\sin\left[\frac{\pi}{6}(4-2)\right]+48=22\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)+48

=22\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)+48=\frac{22\sqrt{3}}{2}+48

So the model gives approximately \boxed{67.1^\circ\text{F}} in April.

data.part_d: What is the phase shift of this function, and what does it mean in this context?
data.part_e: Use the model to estimate the average temperature in March. Round to the nearest tenth of a degree.
data.solution_steps:
Part (a). The midline of a sinusoid f(x)=A\sin[B(x-h)]+D is y=D, and the midline is the average value of the oscillation. Here D=54, so the average temperature is \boxed{54^\circ\text{F}}.

Part (b). The amplitude is A=18, so the quantity rises 18 above the average value and falls 18 below it:

\text{maximum}=54+18=72^\circ\text{F}\qquad\text{minimum}=54-18=36^\circ\text{F}

The warmest month on average is May and the coolest is November, so the range of monthly average temperatures is \boxed{[36^\circ\text{F},\ 72^\circ\text{F}]}.

Part (c). Here B=\frac{\pi}{6}, so the period is

\text{Period}=\frac{2\pi}{B}=\frac{2\pi}{\pi/6}=2\pi\cdot\frac{6}{\pi}=12

The period is \boxed{12} months, and so the temperature pattern repeats every 12 months, that is, once each year.

Part (d). The phase shift is the value of x that makes the argument of the sine equal to zero:

\frac{\pi}{6}(x-2)=0 \implies x-2=0 \implies x=2

The phase shift is \boxed{2} months, and so the sine pattern is shifted 2 months to the right: the temperature is at its average and rising in February, not in January. Equivalently, the warmest month is May and the coolest is November.

Part (e). Substitute x=3 (March):

f(3)=18\sin\left[\frac{\pi}{6}(3-2)\right]+54=18\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)+54

=18\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)+54=63

So the model gives exactly \boxed{63.0^\circ\text{F}} in March.
